target_zone_range.evidence_basis: Hays — Natural Purola flora lists A. viridiflora as naturally occurring. Travis — UT herbarium index includes A. viridiflora. Williamson — county flora includes A. viridiflora.

morphology.look_here_first: Start with the inflorescence position and flower color. Green comet milkweed has tight greenish flower clusters, often from upper leaf axils, with hoods/corona held compactly; leaves are opposite and relatively broad, and the plant lacks the bright green-white spreading flower look of A. viridis.
diagnostic_traits: hoods shorter and more compact than in A. viridis
follicles slender and erect to ascending

comparisons.key_distinctions: A. viridis has larger green-and-white flowers with broad spreading reflexed corolla lobes and more prominent pale hoods. A. viridiflora is more uniformly greenish and compact-flowered.
